title: Intermittent Systems at Small Scale: Execution Model and Design Guidelines
problem: Intermittent systems with small energy storage suffer from reduced power efficiency when designed using traditional execution models that do not accurately capture hardware-level behavior, leading to suboptimal checkpoint mechanisms and unsafe operations.
motivation: Energy-harvesting systems need precise execution models to maximize power efficiency and ensure reliable checkpoint operations amid frequent power failures.
method: The paper proposes an improved execution model that more accurately describes intermittent systems with small energy storage, addressing shortcomings in traditional models. Design guidelines are derived to enhance both static and dynamic checkpoint techniques by accounting for the true power budget and hardware constraints of small-scale systems.
key_novelty: A hardware-accurate execution model for small-scale intermittent systems that reveals significant power efficiency gaps in traditional checkpoint designs.
contributions: Execution model capturing accurate power efficiency behavior of small-scale intermittent systems
Quantification showing systems designed with traditional models achieve 5.62x lower power efficiency than expected
Design guidelines improving static checkpoint performance by 3.04x
Design guidelines improving dynamic checkpoint performance by 2.85x
primary_theme: Execution model accuracy for power-constrained intermittent systems
